post.caption: Harry Winston invented this necklace's name. In 1947, he bought an emerald and diamond necklace from a prince's family and named it the Spanish Inquisition Necklace. The name has no known tie to the Spanish Inquisition. Later tales said Spanish, then French, royalty owned it first, but none of that was ever shown. Katharine Hepburn borrowed it for the 1947 Academy Awards. Winston sold it in 1955, and it went to the Smithsonian in 1972. It holds 15 emeralds, and the largest weighs about 45 carats.
